html:
Tiruchirappalli, often called Trichy, is a city on the Kaveri river in the middle of Tamil Nadu. A fort and temples stand on the Rockfort, a rock that rises about 80 metres above the town.

Uraiyur, now part of the city, was a capital of the early Chola kings, one of the three Tamil kingdoms. On an island in the river just to the north is Srirangam, one of the largest Hindu temples in use. The Nayak rulers of Madurai made the city their capital for parts of the 1600s. In the Carnatic Wars of the 1750s the British, the French and their Indian allies fought over it.

The physicist C. V. Raman was born here in 1888.
